Name: recall_success_dissociation
Title: Recall Ranks Retrievers, Success Does Not: A Two-Environment Audit of Experience Retrieval Against the Static Prompt with Manipulated Duplicate Availability
Short Hypothesis: Retriever recall (fraction of top-k items sharing the test task's type or binding) and the task-success residual over the best static prompt dissociate, and the dissociation is set by whether the retrieved binding is recoverable inside the episode. On ALFWorld, the residual over the best static arm is a step at type recall (random-type retrieval loses, BM25 and an oracle same-scene retriever sit within the floor) and is unchanged when same-scene items are removed from the bank, because object locations are recoverable by looking; on WebShop, where the binding (which product satisfies the attribute set) is expensive to recover by search, the residual appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank and tracks product recall. Recall above the type threshold is therefore uninformative unless the bank carries non-recoverable bindings, and retriever evaluation must report success residual over the static arm at two duplicate-availability levels.
Related Work: 2604.04949 trains retrievers from agent trajectories and reports evidence recall and task success together with no random or fixed control, so recall and success are never dissociated. 2512.20854 correlates retrieval metrics with LLM-judged answer quality in RAG QA and 2508.05909 tries to isolate the retriever's contribution to a reader; both are single-turn QA with no static arm. 2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write strategy on LoCoMo (QA, no full-history or fixed arm). SWE-ContextBench (2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps and mis-selected experience harms on dependency-linked tasks, without a random or static control; 2607.10608 shows wrong retrieved memory is adopted at the first decision point. Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234) and ExpeL/Reflexion report ALFWorld and WebShop memory gains over no memory only. Measurement A on this node observed unseen approximately equal to seen with one retriever and no static arm. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap without manipulating it.
Abstract: Retrievers for agent memory are ranked by recall of relevant items; whether that ranking survives when the outcome is task success over the best static prompt is unknown, and it should depend on whether the retrieved item carries something the agent cannot recover in the episode. We manipulate two things on two environments: retriever recall (random-type, goal-BM25, oracle same-binding, at matched k=3) and the bank's duplicate availability (with versus without items sharing the test task's binding: scene on ALFWorld, goal product on WebShop). Every retrieval cell is reported as the success residual over the best static arm built from the same bank (fixed exemplars, compiled procedure, whole bank where it fits), paired on games and seeds, with Qwen3-32B. The prediction is a dissociation: on ALFWorld the residual is a step at type recall and flat above it, unaffected by removing same-scene items; on WebShop the residual appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank and tracks product recall, and vanishes when duplicates are removed. A positive control (retrieval over no memory clearing the floor on WebShop) gates the second environment. The audit yields a rule for evaluating experience retrievers: report success residual over the static arm under two duplicate-availability levels, and treat recall above the type threshold as uninformative unless the bank carries bindings the episode cannot recover.
Experiments: E0 ALFWorld reuse: A (k=0; BM25 k=3) and C (static arms; the best static arm chosen on pooled cells). E1 ALFWorld retriever ladder at k=3, 274 x 2 each: random-type (uniform over the bank, type recall about 1/6), goal-BM25 (A, type recall about 1), oracle same-type-same-scene on valid_seen (binding recall 1; on valid_unseen it reduces to same-type); C's different-type placebo serves as the recall-0 point; 1,644 episodes (~1.5 h). E2 ALFWorld duplicate manipulation: BM25 k=3 with a per-game bank filter excluding same-scene items on valid_seen, paired with A's k=3; 548 episodes. E3 WebShop setup (one day) and bank: Qwen3-32B run on 3,000 train instructions at k=0; successes form bank-full; per test instruction, bank-dup (full) and bank-nodup (items whose goal product equals the test goal product removed); achieved same-product rates reported (target at least 30% versus 0%); the public human demonstrations are added if the self-success rate is thin. E4 WebShop arms, 500 test instructions x 2 seeds each: k=0; static arms: fixed 3 exemplars (token-matched to k=3), compiled procedure (~80 tokens, written by rule from the bank), whole-bank-in-context up to 16k with shortest-first truncation; retrieval k=3: random, instruction-BM25, oracle same-product, each under bank-dup and bank-nodup (cells that coincide are shared); about 10.5k episodes (~8 h). E5 gate: WebShop BM25 k=3 over k=0 must clear the floor before any residual claim. E6 analysis: for each retriever and bank level, recall@3 (type or category recall; binding recall = same scene or same product) and success residual over the best static arm at that bank level; residual plotted against binding recall for both environments; residual per uncached prefill token reported as the cost axis.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static arms first, per the brief): k=0; fixed 3 exemplars token-matched to k=3; compiled procedure prompt; whole-bank-in-context where it fits; on ALFWorld the C arms including the type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt. Manipulations: retriever ladder (random-type, BM25, oracle same-binding) and bank duplicate availability (dup versus nodup) on both environments. Ablations: k=1 versions of oracle and BM25 on WebShop (residual is not a length effect); type-agnostic procedure-only static on WebShop versus fixed exemplars; random-type retrieval on WebShop with bank-dup (isolates the item content from the binding).
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (ALFWorld step): the residual over the best static arm is at or below minus 8 net for random-type retrieval and within ±8 for BM25 and oracle same-scene. Falsified by an oracle residual above 8 net (scene bindings carry value that the static arm lacks), produced by the oracle arm on valid_seen; or by random-type retrieval within ±8 of the static arm (procedures do not matter, contradicting A), produced by the random-type arm. P2 (ALFWorld manipulation): excluding same-scene items changes the BM25 k=3 residual by less than 8 net. Falsified by a drop of at least 8 net, produced by E2. P3 (WebShop manipulation): under bank-nodup every retriever's residual over the best static arm is within the floor; under bank-dup, oracle same-product and BM25 residuals are at least 8 net with oracle at or above BM25. Falsified by a residual of at least 8 net under bank-nodup (retrieval carries value beyond duplicates, for example category search strategies), produced by the bank-nodup BM25 or oracle arm; or by oracle same-product within the floor under bank-dup (a duplicate trajectory does not transfer the binding), produced by the bank-dup oracle arm. P4 (cross-environment): the slope of residual on binding recall is within the floor on ALFWorld and at least 8 net per unit recall on WebShop under bank-dup. Falsified by same-sign slopes of the same size on both environments, produced by the two ladders jointly. P5 (gate, positive control): WebShop BM25 k=3 beats k=0 by at least the WebShop floor. If falsified, produced by E5, the WebShop side is declared uninformative and P3/P4 are not claimed.

Recall computed per episode from retrieved item ids. Per-category WebShop and per-type ALFWorld results exploratory. Name: whole_bank_confusability_ladder
Title: Confusable, Not Long: The Whole-Bank-in-Context Route Loses to Top-k Retrieval Only as Near-Miss Trajectories Accumulate
Short Hypothesis: On a six-procedure trajectory bank, reading the whole bank as a cached static prefix matches goal-sentence top-3 retrieval on task success up to the 16k context no matter how many redundant or off-domain items are added; it falls below retrieval only as the count of near-miss items (same object and receptacle words, different procedure) grows, whereas retrieval responds to the near-miss share rather than the count. The bank size at which the two routes cross is therefore set by bank composition, not prompt length, and it is smaller for a weaker reader (Qwen3-8B) than for Qwen3-32B.
Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arxiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapsing as the registry grows while retrieve-then-rank degrades gracefully, but scores Match@1 with one router model and grows the number of distinct options, not the number of confusable copies. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) and arxiv:2412.16926 find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the similar examples and that selection matters less as shots grow, on classification tasks; MANYICLBENCH (arxiv:2411.07130) separates similar-sample from all-sample learning; arxiv:2510.16809 finds a few well-chosen examples beating many on code translation. arxiv:2607.26497 measures a corpus-size crossover between agentic search and BM25 on documents with one reader; arxiv:2603.04814 measures Mem0 against long context on conversational QA with one model; arxiv:2411.05000 shows effective context shorter than advertised on synthetic threads. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory; SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reports clutter from larger libraries under an unspecified selection. None of these grows a trajectory bank while holding the procedure count fixed and separating redundant count, off-domain length and confusable count, scores task success, and checks whether the crossover moves with the reader.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers assume a bank of trajectories must be queried because the whole bank will not fit or will not be read well, and the long-context literature reports crossovers between retrieval and in-context reading measured on documents with one reader. We ask what property of a trajectory bank actually makes the whole-bank-in-context route fall behind top-k retrieval on task success. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we grow a six-item seed bank (one expert exemplar per task type) to 12, 24, 48 and 80 items in three ways that hold the six procedures fixed: redundant growth (same-type items whose object-receptacle pairs collide with no other type), off-domain filler (token-matched trajectories from another text game), and near-miss growth (every added item has a twin of another type with the same object and receptacle, so half the bank is confusable). Each bank is read whole as a cached static prefix or through goal-sentence top-3 retrieval, on the same 274 games and two seeds, with the Measurement C static arms as the baseline and a fixed uniformly random 80-item subset as the selection control. We predict the whole-bank route is flat under redundant and filler growth and declines with the near-miss count, while retrieval declines with near-miss share only, so the crossover in items depends on composition and arrives earlier for Qwen3-8B. Prefill tokens and GPU-seconds under prefix caching are logged for accuracy-cost curves.
Experiments:
- Bank construction from the expert pool (1,465 items). Seed S6 = one expert exemplar per task type, fixed. Growth to 12/24/48/80 items under three rules that keep six procedures: R (redundant, near-miss share 0): add same-type items whose (object, receptacle) pair appears in no item of another type in the bank; N (near-miss, share 0.5): add items in cross-type twin pairs (same object and receptacle, different procedure; twins chosen so their first actions coincide), so at every size half of the items have a twin in the bank; F (filler, sizes 24/48/80 only): S6 plus token-matched trajectories from public TextWorld cooking games in the same format with no ALFWorld nouns. U: one uniformly random fixed 80-subset of the pool (natural near-miss share, measured and reported) as the G17 fixed-random-selection control. Item order type-interleaved, fixed per arm.
- Routes. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic static prefix (vLLM prefix caching on, cache hit ratio logged). RET: goal-sentence top-3 from the same bank per episode (uncached), same retriever as Measurement A. For every bank both routes run on the same 274 games x 2 seeds.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B: WB x {R,N} x 5 sizes (10), RET x {R,N} x 5 sizes (10), WB x F x 3 sizes (3), WB x U (1); RET on the full pool is Measurement A k=3 (on disk). 24 new arms; WB arms at 48/80 items run 2-3x slower per episode, so about 16 h on two GPUs with one replica each and arms interleaved across replicas.
- Reader manipulation (G16): Qwen3-8B on WB and RET x {R,N} x {12,48,80} (12 arms) plus 8B k=0 and 8B three fixed type-conditioned exemplars (2 arms), about 4 h. Crossover size per reader = smallest size at which WB minus RET is at or below -8 net on the N ladder.
- Error signature: in failed episodes, the fraction in which the executed action sequence follows the twin's procedure (skipped or inserted clean/heat/cool step) is read from the action log, per route and size, to show that the decline is procedure confusion rather than generic length failure.
- Cost: GPU-seconds per episode at fixed concurrency (16 workers per replica), prefill tokens per episode, cache hit ratio; accuracy-cost curves per route and size; the cost crossover is reported separately from the accuracy crossover.
- Order: positive control first (Measurement C wrong-type placebo must sit at least 8 net below the right-type single exemplar, pooled over twin-bearing types); pre-registration; R and N ladders at 32B; then F, U, order re-shuffle check at N-48; then Qwen3-8B.
Baselines and Ablations:
- k=0 (Measurement A) and the five Measurement C static arms: one and three fixed type-conditioned exemplars, wrong-type fixed exemplar (length placebo and near-miss positive control), per-type procedure paragraph, six-procedure type-agnostic prompt; every retrieval number is reported as retrieval minus the best of these at matched tokens.
- RET k=3 over the natural pool (Measurement A) and RET with random fixed selection (three random items from the same bank, fixed per game) at the same token budget, to separate the retriever from the exemplar budget.
- WB x F filler ladder isolates prompt length from content; WB x U fixed random 80-subset is the matched-budget random-selection control at the whole-context budget and supplies a third, natural near-miss share.
- Order ablation (exploratory): N-48 with a second type-interleaved shuffle, to bound order effects that could mimic composition effects.
- Reader ablation: Qwen3-8B on both ladders at three sizes.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (length does not hurt): WB on the R ladder stays within +/-8 net of WB at S6 through 80 items, and WB on the F ladder stays within +/-8 of S6 at matched tokens. Falsified if WB(R-80) or WB(F-80) is at least 8 net below WB(S6) on the paired cells; arm: WB R-80 and WB F-80 vs WB S6.
- P2 (confusable count hurts the whole-bank route): WB on the N ladder declines monotonically and WB(N-80) minus WB(N-6) is at or below -9 net (one third of the Gate-0 gain), with the decline carried by twin-procedure errors in the action log. Falsified if WB(N-80) is within +/-8 of WB(N-6), or if the decline is not accompanied by a rise in twin-procedure errors; arm: WB N-80 vs WB N-6.
- P3 (retrieval responds to share, not count): RET(N-48) is at least 8 net below RET(R-48), and RET(N-80) is within +/-8 of RET(N-12). Falsified either if RET(N-48) is within +/-8 of RET(R-48) (the retriever is immune to twins, so share does not matter) or if RET declines with size at fixed share; arms: RET N-48 vs RET R-48, RET N-80 vs RET N-12.
- P4 (interaction): [WB(N-80) - WB(N-6)] - [RET(N-80) - RET(N-12)] is at or below -9 net. Falsified if the two routes decline by the same amount (within 8 net) on the N ladder; arms: the four cells named.
- P5 (crossover moves with reader): on the N ladder Qwen3-8B's crossover size is smaller than Qwen3-32B's (8B crosses at 48 or earlier when 32B crosses at 80 or not at all). Falsified if 8B crosses at the same size or later than 32B, or if 8B shows no crossover while 32B does; arms: 8B WB N-48/N-80 vs 8B RET N-48/N-80, against the 32B cells.
- P6 (fixed random selection): WB(U-80) is within +/-8 of RET k=3 on the full pool (Measurement A). Falsified if WB(U-80) is at least 8 net below Measurement A k=3; arm: WB U-80.
Measurement and Noise Control: All arms run the same 274 games (140 valid_seen + 134 valid_unseen) x 2 seeds with identical seeds across arms; every contrast is a paired net difference with the +/-8 net floor at 274 x 2; confirmatory effects must exceed the floor and be at least one third of the Gate-0 retrieval gain (+27 net at k=3). Crossover size is defined before the run as the smallest ladder size at which WB minus RET is at or below -8 net. Per-type claims are made only on the pooled twin-bearing types (clean, heat, cool, pick-and-place) and declared exploratory. Positive control before any null: the Measurement C wrong-type placebo must be at least 8 net below the right-type single exemplar; if it is not, the near-miss manipulation has no leverage and the design stops. Order sensitivity is bounded by the N-48 re-shuffle cell. Cost is measured, not modelled: GPU-seconds per episode at fixed concurrency with prefix caching on, prefill tokens and cache hit ratio per episode, reported as accuracy-cost curves. Qwen3-8B k=0 is run first; if 8B's k=0 to k=3 gain is below the floor the reader arm is reported as uninformative rather than as a null crossover. Pre-registration after the positive control.

Name: many_shot_averages_detours
Title: Reading the Whole Bank Averages Out Detours: Many-Shot Context Is Robust to Per-Item Noise Where Top-k Retrieval Commits to It
Short Hypothesis: When the bank holds the agent's own successful-but-detoured trajectories (self pool) instead of expert trajectories, top-k retrieval passes the detours of the k items it commits to into the episode (more steps, more step-limit failures, lower success), while the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate because the shared procedure is the consensus across many noisy items; the gap between routes grows with the bank's detour rate and with item count, and closes when detours are pruned from the items.
Related Work: Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) report that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the most similar examples rather than cumulative learning, and arxiv:2412.16926 that long-context models are less sensitive to example selection; both predict that a whole-bank prompt inherits whatever its most similar item contains, the opposite of consensus reading. In-context learning with noisy labels (arxiv:2411.19581) and many-shot ICL (arxiv:2404.11018, including Unsupervised and Reinforced ICL with model-generated examples) study label noise in classification, not action noise in trajectories. ExpeL and SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reuse raw on-policy trajectories and report episode-specific drift and clutter from larger libraries without stating how items were selected; Honest Lying (arxiv:2605.29463) shows reflexive agents storing confident wrong interpretations; MemoryGraft (arxiv:2512.16962) and the compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) show agents imitating implanted or conflicting retrieved experiences. None sets the detour rate of a trajectory bank at several levels and compares whole-bank reading with top-k retrieval on task success and steps.
Abstract: Long-context in-context learning studies report that gains from many demonstrations come from attention to the most similar examples rather than from cumulative learning, which predicts that reading a whole bank of trajectories inherits whatever the most similar item contains. We test the opposite on agent trajectories, where per-item noise has a natural form: the detours in the agent's own successful episodes. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we build banks from the expert pool (no detours), the self pool (every item detoured), a 50/50 mix, a pruned self pool whose non-causal steps are removed by rule and re-validated by replay, and an amplified self pool drawn from the longest detours. Each bank is read by goal-sentence top-3 retrieval or whole in a cached prefix at 6, 24 and 48 items, on the same 274 games and two seeds, scoring success, steps and step-limit failures against the Measurement C static arms. We predict retrieval passes detours into the episode, that the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate and improves with item count on the self pool only, and that pruning restores retrieval. A per-episode imitation signature (episode steps against the injected items' detour steps) separates consensus reading from most-similar-item copying. Costs under caching are measured, since the robust route is also the longer prefix.
Experiments:
- Pools and banks. E: expert pool (1,465). S: self pool (1,892 successes). Detour measure per item = steps beyond the expert solution length for the same game; distribution reported. M: 50/50 mix by type. P: pruned S, removing visits to receptacles that did not yield the target object and repeated identical actions, then replaying the pruned action list in the same game and keeping only replays that still succeed (pruned items are therefore valid successful trajectories). A: S items from the top tercile of detour steps within each type. Item tokens measured (E about 140; S expected about 2x).
- Routes. RET: goal-sentence top-3 from each bank (same retriever as Measurement A), uncached; retrieved item lengths and detour steps logged per episode. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic cached static prefix at 6, 24 and 48 items (48 S items must fit 16k with game history; otherwise 40 under a fixed type-balanced subset rule, stated before the run). Token-matched comparison WB E-48 vs WB S-24 also reported.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B: RET x {S, M, P, A} (RET E is Measurement A); WB x {E6, E24, E48, S6, S24, S48, M48, P48}. About 12 arms, roughly 8 h on two GPUs.
- Outcomes: success (primary), steps per episode and step-limit failures (secondary, paired). Imitation signature: for RET arms, the per-game paired difference in episode steps between S and E injections regressed on the injected items' detour steps; for WB arms, the same regression on the detour steps of the most similar item in the prefix (by the retriever's score) and on the bank-mean detour steps, to tell most-similar copying from consensus.
- Reader: Qwen3-8B on RET E, RET S, WB48 E, WB48 S as an exploratory replication of the 2x2 (4 arms).
- Cost: prefill tokens, GPU-seconds per episode under prefix caching; detours lengthen episodes and multiply decode steps, so cost per success is reported for both routes.
- Order: positive control first (RET A vs RET E); pre-registration; then the 2x2 (RET/WB x E/S at 48); then the S ladder, M and P; then Qwen3-8B.
Baselines and Ablations:
- k=0 and the Measurement C static arms (fixed type-conditioned exemplars, wrong-type placebo, procedure paragraph, six-procedure prompt); every retrieval number is reported as retrieval minus the best static arm at matched tokens.
- RET E (Measurement A) is the clean-item reference; RET with random fixed selection of three S items per game separates the retriever from the detour content.
- Pruned bank P is the repair ablation; amplified bank A is the positive control for imitation; mix M gives the intermediate detour rate.
- WB E ladder (6/24/48) is the no-noise reference for the item-count dose-response on S.
- Token-matched WB E-48 vs WB S-24 controls for the longer S items.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (retrieval inherits detours): RET S minus RET E is at or below -8 net and RET S episodes are longer by at least 2 steps on the paired median. Falsified if RET S is within +/-8 of RET E with no step increase; arm: RET S vs RET E.
- P2 (route x noise interaction, headline): [WB48 S - WB48 E] - [RET S - RET E] is at least +9 net. Falsified if both routes lose the same amount within 8 net, or if WB48 S loses more than RET S (the most-similar-item copying outcome predicted by arxiv:2405.00200); arms: the four cells WB48 E, WB48 S, RET E, RET S.
- P3 (dose-response in item count on noisy items): WB S rises from 6 to 48 items by at least 9 net while WB E is flat within +/-8 over the same ladder. Falsified if WB6 S is within 8 net of WB48 S or above it; arms: WB S6, S24, S48 vs WB E6, E24, E48.
- P4 (pruning repairs retrieval): RET P is within +/-8 of RET E and at least 9 net above RET S. Falsified if RET P is still at least 8 net below RET E, which would locate the deficit in something other than detours (phrasing, length); arm: RET P.
- P5 (positive control): RET A is at least 8 net below RET S and its episodes are the longest. Falsified if RET A is within +/-8 of RET E, in which case imitation has no leverage and the design stops; arm: RET A.
- P6 (mechanism): in RET arms episode steps rise with the injected items' detour steps (paired slope above zero at the 95% paired-bootstrap level), while in WB48 S episode steps do not rise with the most-similar item's detour steps. Falsified if WB48 S episodes track the most-similar item's detours as strongly as RET episodes track theirs; arm: WB48 S with per-item similarity and detour steps logged.
- P7 (mix): WB48 M is within +/-8 of WB48 E while RET M sits between RET E and RET S. Falsified if WB48 M is at least 8 net below WB48 E; arms: WB48 M, RET M.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired cells on 274 games x 2 seeds with identical seeds across arms; +/-8 net floor; confirmatory effects must exceed the floor and be at least one third of the Gate-0 retrieval gain (+27 net at k=3). Steps and step-limit failures are paired per game and summarised by median differences with paired-bootstrap intervals. Per-type results pooled over the three procedure-heavy types (clean, heat, cool) and declared exploratory. Positive control before any null: RET A must be at least 8 net below RET E. Success ceiling (0.87 at k=7) limits headroom for success, so steps are the pre-registered secondary outcome on which the imitation claim can still be tested. Item lengths and retrieved-item lengths are logged to rule out a retriever length bias explaining RET S. Cost measured as GPU-seconds per episode and prefill tokens under prefix caching. Pre-registration after the positive control.

Name: near_duplicate_needle_crossover
Title: Bigger Banks Help Retrieval Only Through Near-Duplicates the Reader Cannot Find in Context: Bank Size x Near-Duplicate Rate on WebShop and ALFWorld
Short Hypothesis: The growth of top-k retrieval's advantage over the whole-bank-in-context route with bank size is a near-duplicate effect: with instance-level near-duplicates removed from the bank, retrieval and whole-bank are within the noise floor at every bank size on both environments; with near-duplicates planted at a controlled rate, retrieval's gain rises with the rate on WebShop (one procedure, instance-specific bindings) and the whole-bank route recovers only part of it, the recovered fraction falling as the haystack grows from 12 to 40 items; on ALFWorld (procedure-bound) the same manipulation moves neither route.
Related Work: Synapse (arxiv:2306.07863) introduced trajectory-as-exemplar prompting with state abstraction and an exemplar memory retrieved by similarity on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web, without a whole-bank or random-selection control; ExpeL and Agent Workflow Memory likewise assume retrieval over experience on WebShop-style tasks. arxiv:2603.18272 trains agents to use retrieved trajectories without a fixed or random exemplar control. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to similar examples so that random many-shot converges to retrieval on classification, and arxiv:2412.16926 that selection matters less with long context; arxiv:2411.05000 shows in-context lookup degrading with context on synthetic threads. arxiv:2607.26497 sweeps corpus size on documents with one reader and scores recall. The archived order_randomized_leakage_audit observed near-duplicate leakage in task streams, and decorative_retriever observed that retrieval-set overlap predicts retrieval necessity; neither planted or removed near-duplicates or ran a whole-bank arm.
Abstract: Bank-size sweeps in retrieval are done on document corpora with one reader and scored on recall; for agent experience banks the operative question is why a larger bank helps retrieval at all, and whether the whole bank in context would do the same. We hypothesise that the bank-size curve of top-k retrieval on trajectory banks is a near-duplicate coverage curve, and that the whole-bank route's curve is an in-context lookup curve that falls as the haystack grows. On WebShop, a bindings-bound environment (one procedure, instance-specific product and option choices), we build per-cluster banks of state-abstracted successful trajectories at 12 and 40 items in which the fraction of test instructions with an instance-level near-duplicate (same product, or same category with two shared attributes) is set to 0, 0.5 or 1, and read them by instruction-text top-2 retrieval, whole in a cached prefix, or through fixed two-exemplar and compiled-procedure static prompts. The same manipulation with same-scene, same-type trajectories is run on ALFWorld. We predict no retrieval residual over the whole bank without near-duplicates on either environment, a residual that grows with the planted rate on WebShop only, and a whole-bank recovery of that residual below half that shrinks from 12 to 40 items. Task success is primary, the near-duplicate hit rate a mediator, and cost is measured under prefix caching.
Experiments:
- WebShop setup (public data, one day). Reader Qwen3-32B. Evaluation on the standard 500 test instructions x 2 seeds; k=0 and a k=0 seed-replicate first to set the paired floor.
- Bank material: successes (reward 1.0) of Qwen3-32B on at least 2,000 train instructions (expected 600-800 items) plus the public human demonstrations; state abstraction in the Synapse style (search-result pages reduced to item id, title and price lines; product pages to title, price, options and the buy action), applied identically to retrieved and whole-bank items; item length measured (target about 300 tokens).
- Near-duplicate definition for a test instruction: a bank trajectory whose instruction targets the same product id, or the same category with at least two shared attribute phrases; the near-duplicate gain is also reported as a function of the number of shared attributes. Cluster design: the 500 test instructions are partitioned by category into about 42 clusters of about 12; each cluster gets one static bank per (size, rate) cell, cached across the cluster's episodes. At size 40 and rate 1 the bank holds one near-duplicate per cluster instruction plus 28 non-duplicate items; rate 0.5 holds six; rate 0 holds 40 non-duplicates. At size 12 and rate 1 the bank is the 12 near-duplicates (each instruction's needle among 11 same-category siblings); rate 0 holds 12 non-duplicates. Non-duplicate items are drawn from other categories.
- Routes: WB-12, WB-40 (cluster bank as a cached static prefix); RET-2 (top-2 from the same cluster bank by BM25 plus embedding over instruction text, uncached; near-duplicate hit rate in the top-2 logged); static arms: fixed two random non-duplicate exemplars for all clusters (cached), one compiled procedure paragraph (search, pick, options, buy; cached), k=0.
- WebShop arms: WB x {12,40} x r{0,0.5,1} (6), RET x {12,40} x r{0,0.5,1} (6), fixed-2, compiled, k=0 x2 (4): 16 arms x 1,000 episodes, about 1 h each on two GPUs; bank generation about 2 h.
- ALFWorld: near-duplicate = same-scene, same-type expert trajectory (bindings: object location in that scene); applies to the 140 valid_seen games, with the 134 valid_unseen games as the no-near-duplicate reference within the same arm. Name: state_key_pays_only_for_planted_bindings
Title: What the Query Can Index: Observation-Keyed Retrieval Beats Goal-Keyed Retrieval and the Best Static Prompt Only When the Bank Carries Scene-Keyed Bindings at a Controlled Rate
Short Hypothesis: The residual of experience retrieval over the best static prompt equals the within-type variance in the bank that the query key can index and a fixed prompt cannot. On ALFWorld the goal sentence already reveals type and object class, so a goal-keyed retriever cannot index anything a type-conditioned static prompt lacks, whereas an observation-keyed retriever can index scene identity. We plant scene-keyed bindings (where the target object is in this scene) into the bank for 0/25/50/100 percent of evaluation games and predict: every key's residual is inside the +/-8-net floor at 0 percent; the residual rises with the rate for the observation key only; a compact whole-binding table in a cached static prompt matches observation-keyed retrieval at 100 percent; and a wrong planted binding costs more than a right one gains.
Related Work: Synapse (arXiv:2306.07863) keys trajectory exemplars by abstracted state but never compares the state key against a goal key or a matched-length static prompt and does not manipulate whether the bank holds state-keyed content. FocusMem (arXiv:2608.04530) adds state-conditioned retrieval with a trust gate for GUI agents with the same omissions. RAP (arXiv:2402.03610) retrieves by current situation with no static or goal-keyed control. arXiv:2603.18272 trains the reader (LoRA) to use retrieved trajectories with a fixed goal query and no random or fixed control. ICAL (arXiv:2406.14596) reports no fixed-set control. Measurement A on this node found unseen ~ seen, i.e. no scene component in the retrieved value; this proposal manufactures that component at four rates. Archived compile_dont_retrieve (6.0) called the query-conditioned read inert without manipulating the property that would make it non-inert; decorative_retriever (5.75) observed overlap only. Cross-axis: arXiv:2607.10608 (compliance) motivates the wrong-binding arm; arXiv:2603.04814 and arXiv:2506.03989 motivate the cached whole-table arm.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers report the gain of a retriever over no memory, rarely over a fixed prompt built from the same experience, and never as a function of what the query key can index. We formalise the retrieval residual as the within-type variance of the bank that is indexable by the key but not by a static prompt, and test it on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds per cell, k=3, token-matched to +/-5 percent) by crossing three keys (goal sentence, initial observation, current observation at first stall) with a bank in which scene-keyed binding items ('scene signature S: object O was found in receptacle R', ~30 tokens, derived from the game's PDDL) are planted for r in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of evaluation games, fixed per game across seeds and keys; a natural-binding level built from same-floorplan train trajectories, whose correctness rate is measured, and a wrong-binding level (100 percent incorrect receptacle) complete the ladder. Baselines are the best type-conditioned static arm and the type-agnostic static arm from Measurement C (re-run on the same seeds for test-retest), random-within-type selection at matched length, a whole-binding-table static prompt (all 274 rows, ~8k tokens, one cached prefix for the arm) at r=0.5 and 1.0, and oracle injection of the game's own binding as the positive control. Prefill tokens per episode are logged per arm so cached static prefixes and uncached retrieved prefixes give an accuracy-cost frontier. Predictions: at r=0 no key exceeds the best static arm by more than 8 net; the observation-key residual rises with r to at least half the Gate-0 gain at r=1.0 while the goal-key residual stays inside the floor; the cached whole-table prompt matches observation-keyed retrieval; and the wrong-binding harm exceeds the right-binding gain. The result is a pre-registered rule for when a query is necessary: only when a bank statistic (variance within type that the key can index) is non-zero, and the amount is measured rather than named.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld valid_seen and valid_unseen (274 games), 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms; Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas (one per GPU, prefix caching on); k=3 (~430 tokens); a planted binding item replaces the same number of exemplar tokens so all arms are matched to +/-5 percent (verified from logged prefill counts). Bank manipulation: binding item = 'Scene signature <sorted receptacle inventory of the first observation>: <object class> was found in <receptacle>' (~30 tokens); planted from the game's PDDL for a random fraction r in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of games (assignment fixed per game across seeds and keys); natural level = same-floorplan train-split expert trajectories with their measured correctness rate p_nat (a fifth, uncontrolled rate); wrong level = plausible but incorrect receptacle for 100 percent of games. Query manipulation: goal key (goal sentence; BM25 and bge-m3 dense, index over trajectories plus binding items), initial-observation key (first observation text), stall key (current observation at the first repeated or 'Nothing happens' action, retrieved items appended as a new message so the cached prefix survives), random-within-type at matched length. Static arms: best type-conditioned static (3 fixed exemplars + procedure) and type-agnostic static (six procedures) from Measurement C, re-run; whole-binding-table static (type-agnostic prompt + all 274 rows, ~8k tokens, one cached prefix) at r=0.5 (137 true rows, the reader must find its row or ignore the table) and r=1.0. Positive control: oracle injection of the game's own binding. Cells: 3 keys x 4 rates (12) + random x {0, 1.0} (2) + wrong-binding x {goal, observation} (2) + whole-table x 2 + oracle (1) + natural x {goal, observation} (2) + 2 static re-runs = 23 cells, ~30 min each, ~6 h wall-clock with both GPUs saturated (episode workers tuned to the vLLM running queue >= 8 per replica). Order (pre-registered): static re-runs and oracle first (test-retest floor and positive control), then the rate ladder for the observation key, then the goal and stall keys, then wrong and natural levels. Cost: uncached prefill tokens per episode and cache hit rate per arm from vLLM logs; report accuracy vs uncached tokens. Ablations: scene signature as receptacle-inventory hash vs raw first-observation text; k=1 vs k=3 for the observation key at r=1.0; Qwen3-8B reader on the r=1.0 cells (exploratory). WebShop is out of scope for this claim (no scene structure); the bank statistic proposed for prediction is the fraction of items whose content varies within type conditional on the key.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: best type-conditioned static arm and type-agnostic static arm (Measurement C, re-run on the same seeds); goal-keyed top-3 retrieval (Measurement A, re-run at r=0); random-within-type at matched length (separates the retriever from having type-relevant content); whole-binding-table cached static prompt (the whole-bank arm for the compact binding sub-bank); oracle binding injection (upper bound). Ablations: key encoder (BM25 vs bge-m3) for the goal and observation keys; scene-signature form; k=1 vs k=3 at r=1.0; stall key vs initial-observation key at r=1.0 (does timing of the state matter when the binding is scene-level); reader size (Qwen3-8B, exploratory); natural vs planted binding at the same measured correctness rate (realism check).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (rate-0 residual): at r=0 each key (goal, initial observation, stall) minus the best static arm lies within +/-8 net on the pooled 274x2 cell. Falsified if any key exceeds the best static arm by more than +8 net at r=0. Arm: the three r=0 retrieval cells against the re-run best static cell; nothing in the design prevents the object-specific exemplars they retrieve from adding success, which is what Measurement C's residual tests, so the outcome is open.
- P2 (key x rate interaction): the observation-key residual over the best static arm rises monotonically with r and reaches at least +13 net (half the Gate-0 gain) at r=1.0; the goal-key residual stays within +/-8 net at every r. Falsified if (a) the observation-key residual at r=1.0 is below +8 net (the key does not index the scene or the reader does not apply the binding), or (b) the goal-key residual at r=1.0 exceeds +8 net (object-class matching alone selects the right scene's row often enough). Arms: observation-key and goal-key cells at r=1.0 and the trend across r=0.25/0.5.
- P3 (whole table vs retrieval): at r=1.0 the whole-binding-table static arm (274 rows, cached) is within +/-8 net of observation-keyed retrieval, and at r=0.5 it is within +/-8 net of observation-keyed retrieval at r=0.5. Falsified if the table arm is below the retrieval arm by more than 8 net at either rate (the reader cannot locate its row among 274, or the 137 rows for other scenes at r=0.5 induce compliance). Arm: the two whole-table cells. Not entailed: the table contains the retrieved row, but whether an 8k-token table lies inside the reader's effective context is empirical and can come out either way.
- P4 (asymmetry): the wrong-binding arm with the observation key is below the r=0 observation-key cell by more than the r=1.0 observation-key cell is above it (harm exceeds gain). Falsified if harm <= gain, or if the wrong binding does not lower success by more than 8 net at all (the reader ignores bindings). Arm: wrong-binding observation-key cell paired with the r=0 and r=1.0 observation-key cells.
- P5 (random-within-type control): at r=1.0 random-within-type selection is within +/-8 net of the goal key and below the observation key by more than 8 net. Falsified if random matches the observation key (the binding is found by chance or the reader exploits something other than the key) or if random is below the goal key by more than 8 net (the goal key carries object-specific value that P1 missed). Arm: random-within-type cell at r=1.0.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) cells with identical seeds across arms; primary outcome task success; net = paired success difference in percentage points over 274x2 episodes; 95 percent CI from a cluster bootstrap over games (2,000 resamples); the +/-8-net floor is pre-registered and margins are stated as fractions of the Gate-0 retrieval gain (+27/+32 net); per-type numbers (+/-13-15) are exploratory. Test-retest: the best static arm is re-run with the same seeds to give the empirical per-cell noise. The rate ladder is tested by a paired linear trend over r with a cluster-bootstrap CI, not by eyeballing four cells. Binding assignment per game is fixed across seeds and keys so rate cells differ only in the bank; the same index code and k serve all keys; token matching within +/-5 percent and prefix-cache hit rate are verified from logs for every arm. Pre-registration of P1-P5 and the arm list before the first confirmatory cell; positive control (oracle injection) must clear +13 net over the best static arm before any null is interpreted.

Name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting
Title: When to Retrieve Is Only a Budget Question: An Oracle-Decision Bound on the Value of Retrieval Timing for Experience Memory, With Failure-Keyed Retrieval at Stall Tested Against Planted Recoveries and a Compiled Rulebook
Short Hypothesis: The value of any retrieval-timing policy (start, on stall, fixed schedule, learned) over always-retrieve is bounded above by the mass of episodes on which retrieval fails but the cached static prompt succeeds. We measure that bound directly with an oracle-decision arm that retrieves exactly on the (game, seed) episodes the static prompt fails and predict it is inside the +/-8-net floor on ALFWorld, so stall-triggered retrieval can only re-trade uncached tokens for the same success. A failure-keyed query at stall beats a goal-keyed query only when the bank contains matching recovery segments (planted at 100 percent), not with the natural self pool, and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached static prompt matches it.
Related Work: arXiv:2607.24010 (When Should Active RAG Retrieve?) recasts active retrieval as marginal correctness over the no-retrieval answer under a budget, but on QA with document retrieval, without an oracle-decision arm on paired seeds, a stall trigger or caching costs. ProactAgent (arXiv:2604.20572, 'Ask Only When Needed') retrieves proactively from memory and skills for lifelong agents without an always-retrieve-at-matched-cost arm or an upper bound on the decision. FLARE (arXiv:2305.06983) and Adaptive-RAG (arXiv:2403.14403) trigger retrieval by uncertainty or complexity in QA. Reflexion (arXiv:2303.11366) conditions on failure across trials, not within-episode stalls, and has no static control. Digest: arXiv:2607.07380 (hidden-state uncertainty decides when to retrieve; no always/never baselines), s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (RL proxy decides when/how; cost unaccounted), arXiv:2510.16724 (survey; no common protocol), arXiv:2607.20972 (cue-triggered deterministic injection beats voluntary reads; no oracle bound or compiled control), arXiv:2505.00234 (self-generated examples for sequential decision tasks, the on-policy bank). Archived ideas do not address timing; compile_dont_retrieve concerns the goal-conditioned read at episode start.
Abstract: Adaptive retrieval papers ask when to retrieve but do not report what a perfect answer to that question would be worth. For experience memory under prompt caching the accounting is simple: retrieving always costs one uncached prefill of k items per episode; retrieving on some episodes costs proportionally less; and the only way a timing policy can add success over always-retrieve is on episodes where retrieval hurts an episode the static prompt would have solved. We measure that mass on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, expert bank, k=3) with an oracle-decision arm that runs the cached static prompt where the static re-run succeeded and goal-keyed retrieval where it failed, and compare it with always-retrieve at start (Measurement A), the best static arm (Measurement C), a fixed-step schedule, and stall-triggered retrieval (first repeated or 'Nothing happens' action, thresholds 2 and 5) with retrieved items appended so the cached prefix survives. We then ask whether the query at stall matters: goal, current observation, or failure text (last three actions and observations), over the expert pool (no failures), the self pool (1,892 successes with detours, indexed by their failed-action windows), and a planted-recovery bank in which each ALFWorld failure mode has a ~40-token recovery item, with random-at-stall at matched length and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached static prompt as the static counterpart. Predictions: the oracle bound is inside the floor; stall retrieval matches always-retrieve while firing on at most half the episodes; failure-keyed retrieval beats goal-keyed retrieval only with planted recoveries (positive control) and not with the natural self pool; and the rulebook matches planted retrieval at lower uncached cost. The output is an accuracy-cost frontier in which the timing decision moves along the frontier rather than above it, and a test of whether any query is more than decorative at stall time.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: ALFWorld 274 games x 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching, k=3 goal-keyed retrieval (~430 tokens), best static arm from C. Re-runs: static (test-retest floor) and always-retrieve at start. Oracle-decision arm: per (game, seed), static if the static re-run succeeded, else retrieval at start; its difference from always-retrieve estimates P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) minus test-retest loss, read off the 2x2 paired contingency table. Stall trigger: first occurrence of (a) 'Nothing happens' twice in a row or (b) a repeated (observation, action) pair; thresholds 2 and 5 consecutive invalid actions; retrieved items appended as a new environment-style message; a fixed-step schedule arm retrieves at step 10 regardless. Query at stall: goal sentence; current observation; failure key (last three actions and observations). Banks: expert pool; self pool with detour windows indexed; planted-recovery bank (five ALFWorld failure modes: closed receptacle, wrong receptacle, object already held, wrong object instance, missing 'go to'; ~40-token recovery item keyed by failure text; 100 percent coverage); random-at-stall at matched length. Compiled control: recovery rulebook (the five items concatenated into the type-agnostic static prompt, ~200 tokens, cached), alone and with stall retrieval on top. Cells: static re-run, always re-run, oracle, fixed-step schedule, stall(threshold 2) x {goal, observation, failure} x {expert, self} (6), stall failure-key on planted bank, stall random, rulebook static, rulebook + planted stall retrieval, stall threshold 5 goal-key = 16 cells, ~30 min each, ~4 h with both GPUs busy. Logging: firing rate and step-at-fire for stall arms; uncached prefill tokens and cache hit rate per episode per arm; accuracy vs uncached tokens per episode as the cost axis. Order (pre-registered): re-runs and oracle first, then the planted positive control, then the self-pool and rulebook cells, then thresholds and schedule.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: never-retrieve = best static arm (cached); always-retrieve at start (uncached, Measurement A re-run); fixed-step schedule (timing without a trigger); random-at-stall at matched length (content-free trigger); compiled recovery rulebook (static counterpart of failure-keyed retrieval); oracle-decision arm (upper bound on any timing policy). Ablations: stall threshold 2 vs 5; k=1 vs k=3 at stall (exploratory); self-pool indexing of whole trajectories vs detour windows only; failure key with vs without the current observation; rulebook with vs without stall retrieval on top.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (oracle bound): oracle-decision minus always-retrieve is within +/-8 net. Falsified if the oracle exceeds always-retrieve by 8 net or more, which occurs when retrieval fails on at least 8 percent of episodes the static prompt solves (look-at-in-light's -4.8 in Measurement A makes this producible). Arm: the oracle-decision cell against the always-retrieve re-run. Not entailed: on static-success episodes the oracle re-runs static and can lose test-retest cases while always-retrieve can succeed on those same episodes, so the difference can take either sign.
- P2 (stall as budgeting): stall-triggered goal-keyed retrieval (threshold 2, expert pool) is within +/-8 net of always-retrieve while firing on at most 50 percent of episodes. Falsified if it is below always-retrieve by more than 8 net (the stall arrives after the step budget is spent) or fires on more than 50 percent of episodes. Arm: the threshold-2 goal-key stall cell and its firing log. The fixed-step schedule cell adds a second test: if the schedule matches the stall trigger within +/-8 while firing on 100 percent of episodes, the trigger has no value beyond its firing rate, which is the claimed direction; the falsifier is the schedule falling below the stall trigger by more than 8 net.
- P3 (failure key needs matching content, positive control): failure-keyed retrieval from the planted-recovery bank at stall exceeds goal-keyed retrieval from the expert pool at stall by at least 8 net. Falsified if the difference is below 8 net (the failure text does not index the recovery, or the reader does not apply it at stall time). Arm: planted failure-key stall cell vs expert goal-key stall cell. If P3 fails, P4 is uninterpretable and is reported as such.
- P4 (natural self pool is decorative for the failure key): failure-keyed retrieval from the self pool at stall is within +/-8 net of goal-keyed retrieval from the expert pool at stall and of random-at-stall. Falsified if it exceeds either by more than 8 net (the agent's own detours are load-bearing content). Arm: self-pool failure-key stall cell against the expert goal-key stall cell and the random-at-stall cell.
- P5 (rulebook matches retrieval): the compiled recovery rulebook (cached) is within +/-8 net of planted failure-keyed retrieval at stall, and adding stall retrieval on top of the rulebook adds less than 8 net. Falsified if retrieval beats the rulebook by 8 net or more (recovery must be delivered at the moment of failure rather than read from the prefix), or if rulebook + retrieval exceeds rulebook by 8 net or more. Arm: rulebook cell and rulebook + planted stall retrieval cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) cells with identical seeds; primary outcome task success; net differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs over games; +/-8-net floor pre-registered, margins as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32). The oracle bound is computed from the paired 2x2 table of (static success, retrieval success) per episode with a McNemar-style CI, and the static re-run gives the test-retest disagreement that the oracle arm inherits. Stall arms log firing rate and step-at-fire; cost is uncached prefill tokens per episode from vLLM logs, with cache hit rate verified for the static and rulebook arms. Positive controls (Measurement A's always-retrieve gain, P3's planted recovery) must clear the floor before P1, P2, P4 or P5 nulls are interpreted. Pre-registration of P1-P5 and arm order before the first confirmatory cell; per-type numbers exploratory.

Name: rank_flat_retriever_is_a_type_classifier
Title: Rank-Flat Retrieval: Within-Type Similarity Rank and Near-Duplicate Removal Do Not Move Task Success, So the Experience Retriever Reduces to a Type Classifier Plus a Similarity-Scaled Compliance Hazard
Short Hypothesis: On trajectory banks the retriever's contribution to task success is a step function of type match: replacing the top-3 items with items at within-type similarity rank 10-12 or 50-52, or removing every bank item that shares the test game's (type, object, receptacle) or (type, object), changes success by less than the +/-8-net floor, while removing the type drops success to the wrong-type placebo. On the harm side, the most similar wrong-type item hurts more than a random wrong-type item, and the harm is content-driven: relabelling the same items as retrieved memory, examples or instructions changes nothing, whereas an explicit mismatch warning reduces it. A per-type cached sub-bank of up to 80 items therefore matches top-3 retrieval at lower uncached cost.
Related Work: KATE (Liu et al. 2021) and EPR (Rubin et al. 2021) established kNN demonstration selection over random for classification and generation; Rank-ICL (ICTIR 2026) finds ranking-based selection beneficial but not uniformly superior to random; CoDR (arXiv:2511.08977) and gradient-matching selection (arXiv:2506.04579) optimise selection without a within-class rank ladder; arXiv:2512.04106 reports retrieved > random on one model and task with no fixed set. ExpeL (arXiv:2308.10144) retrieves successful trajectories by task similarity on ALFWorld with no rank or leave-out ladder; ExpGraph (arXiv:2605.30712) ranks by utility with no matched random control; arXiv:2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write on LoCoMo by recall, not action; arXiv:2505.15561 finds passage order no better than shuffling. The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows conflicting memory is adopted at the first decision point but does not vary the wrong item's similarity or framing and does not measure the symmetric benefit at matched length; ReMem (arXiv:2511.20857) leaves near-duplicate dependence untested. Abstract: If the value of experience retrieval on a template environment is the type's procedure, the retriever is a type classifier and everything it does beyond that is decorative or harmful. We test this on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, k=3, token-matched to +/-5 percent) with two manipulations of what the retriever returns and one of what the bank contains. The rank ladder replaces the top-3 items with items at within-type bge-m3 similarity rank 10-12, 50-52 and random-within-type. The leave-out ladder rebuilds the index per game after removing items sharing the game's (type, object class, target receptacle), (type, object class), or type, which manipulates near-duplicate availability directly rather than observing it. The harm arms present the most similar wrong-type item (e.g. a heat trajectory for a cool task) against Measurement C's random wrong-type placebo, and present the same wrong items under four headers ('Examples', 'Retrieved from memory of similar past tasks', 'Instructions: follow this procedure', and a mismatch warning) to separate content from framing, with the warning as the positive control that framing can move compliance. A per-type cached sub-bank (all items of the type up to 80, ~11k tokens, six cached prefixes) tests whether a classifier plus a static prefix replaces the retriever entirely. All retrieval cells are reported as differences from the best static arm of Measurement C; retriever metrics (same-object recall, mean similarity) are logged as secondary outcomes to show they move while success does not. Predictions: rank 50-52 is within the floor of rank 1-3; leave-out levels 1 and 2 are within the floor; level 3 falls to the placebo; the most similar wrong item hurts by more than 8 net over the random wrong item; headers do not move success but the warning does; and the cached sub-bank matches top-3. Together these give a measured statement of what an experience retriever is for on a template environment and where its hazard lies.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: 274 games x 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching, k=3 (~430 tokens), items length-matched within +/-5 percent by choosing the nearest-length item inside each rank window. Rank ladder (type-conditioned retrieval, type read from the goal sentence as in Measurement A): ranks 1-3 (Measurement A re-run), 10-12, 50-52, random-within-type; a type-agnostic variant of the top-3 cell retrieves from the whole bank without the type filter. Leave-out ladder: per test game, remove bank items sharing (type, object class id, target receptacle id) [L1], (type, object class id) [L2], type [L3], then retrieve top-3 from the remainder; ALFWorld object class ids are used so synonyms do not leak. Harm arms: most-similar wrong-type items (nearest neighbours among other-type items by bge-m3 similarity to the goal) vs Measurement C's random wrong-type fixed exemplar (re-run); framing cells present the most-similar wrong-type items under 'Examples', 'Retrieved from memory of similar past tasks', 'Instructions: follow this procedure', and 'Examples (may be from a different task; follow only if the task matches)'. Whole-type sub-bank: all items of the game's type up to 80 (truncation rule: shortest first), one cached prefix per type. Static baselines: best type-conditioned static and type-agnostic static from Measurement C, re-run. Cells: rank ladder 4 + type-agnostic top-3 1 + leave-out 3 + harm 2 + framing 3 (the 'Examples' header is the similar-wrong cell) + sub-bank 1 + static re-runs 2 = 16 cells, ~30 min each, ~4 h with both GPUs busy. Secondary outcomes per cell: same-object recall, same-receptacle recall, mean similarity of returned items. Cost: uncached prefill tokens per episode per arm; the sub-bank arm's cache hit rate is verified. Order (pre-registered): static and A re-runs first (test-retest), then harm and warning arms (positive controls), then ladders and sub-bank. Per-type availability of rank-50 items is reported; for types with fewer than 55 items the deepest available rank window is used and declared.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: best type-conditioned static arm and type-agnostic static arm (Measurement C re-runs); top-3 goal-keyed retrieval (Measurement A re-run); random-within-type at matched length; random wrong-type placebo (Measurement C, re-run). Ablations: type-conditioned vs type-agnostic top-3 (is the type filter doing the work); rank window 10-12 vs 50-52; leave-out L1 vs L2 vs L3; similar-wrong vs random-wrong; four framing headers; sub-bank at 40 vs 80 items (exploratory); BM25 vs bge-m3 for the rank ladder (exploratory).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (rank-flat): rank 50-52 within type is within +/-8 net of rank 1-3 on the pooled 274x2 cell. Falsified if rank 1-3 exceeds rank 50-52 by more than 8 net. Arm: the rank-50 cell against the rank-1 re-run. Not entailed: rank within a type varies object and receptacle match, which can carry success.
- P2 (near-duplicate independence): leave-out levels L1 and L2 each change success by less than 8 net relative to the full-bank top-3 cell. Falsified if either drops success by 8 net or more (the gain is carried by near-duplicates). Arm: L1 and L2 cells.
- P3 (type removal): L3 falls to within +/-8 net of the random wrong-type placebo. Falsified if L3 stays more than 8 net above the placebo (cross-type procedure transfers, e.g. heat to cool). Arm: L3 cell against the placebo re-run.
- P4 (similarity-scaled harm): the most-similar wrong-type arm is below the random wrong-type placebo by more than 8 net. Falsified if the difference is below 8 net (compliance does not scale with similarity). Arm: the similar-wrong ('Examples' header) cell against the placebo re-run.
- P5 (framing null with positive control): the 'Retrieved from memory' and 'Instructions' headers are within +/-8 net of the 'Examples' header, while the mismatch-warning header raises success by 8 net or more over 'Examples'. Falsified if either header shifts success by 8 net or more (framing drives compliance), or if the warning fails to shift it (then the null is uninterpretable and is reported as such). Arms: the three framing cells against the 'Examples' cell.
- P6 (per-type cached sub-bank): the whole-type sub-bank (up to 80 items, cached) is within +/-8 net of rank 1-3 with lower uncached prefill per episode. Falsified if it is below rank 1-3 by more than 8 net (many-shot degradation at ~11k tokens). Arm: the sub-bank cell. Not entailed: the sub-bank contains the top-3 items, but whether 80 trajectories inside the reader's context preserve their use is empirical.
- P7 (type filter is the retriever): type-agnostic top-3 retrieval from the whole bank is within +/-8 net of type-conditioned top-3. Falsified if the type-agnostic cell is below the type-conditioned cell by more than 8 net (similarity over the whole bank returns wrong-type items often enough to trigger P4's harm). Arm: the type-agnostic top-3 cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) cells with identical seeds; primary outcome task success; every retrieval cell is also reported as its difference from the best static arm so rank-flatness is anchored to the residual over static; net differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs over games (2,000 resamples); +/-8-net floor pre-registered, margins as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32); per-type numbers exploratory (+/-13-15). Test-retest from the static and A re-runs. Secondary retriever metrics (same-object recall, mean similarity) are reported next to success for every cell so a flat success curve over a steep metric curve is visible. Token matching within +/-5 percent verified from logged prefill counts; item selection inside rank windows is length-matched, not similarity-matched. Positive controls (A's gain over static; P4's harm; P5's warning) must clear the floor before P1, P2 or P5 nulls are interpreted. Pre-registration of P1-P7 and arm order before the first confirmatory cell.

Risk Factors and Limitations: ALFWorld's six templates make the type step coarse and the rank ladder may exhaust distinct items for rare types (pick-two); per-type availability is reported and the deepest available window declared. Leave-out by object class id may still leave functional near-duplicates (same receptacle family); L1 uses receptacle ids to tighten this. Framing effects may depend on the reader's instruction tuning; the warning positive control guards interpretation but the framing result is reader-specific. If the top-3 residual over the best static arm is itself inside the floor (Measurement C), rank-flatness is a bound rather than a decomposition and the harm and sub-bank arms carry the paper. The sub-bank arm's cache hit rate must be verified per type. WebShop is not run; the claim is about template environments, with the bank statistic (items per type, within-type similarity spread) reported for transfer.
Addresses gap: G11 (the retriever's contribution isolated against matched-length random, rank-degraded and near-duplicate-free selection on task success, with a static baseline); secondary G15 (similarity-scaled harm of wrong retrieved items, symmetric benefit at matched length, and whether static or instruction framing induces the same compliance).
